newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium ticks over in physicals, others slower.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium ticks over in physicals, others slower.

text.p: Aluminium business has been ticking over in the European physical market in recent days but other metals have not seen so much activity, traders said.
"Business has been very good in Europe and in the US and in Asia, where Japan premiums are above $85," one aluminium trader said.
But with the LME market now at its highest for 14 months, basis business at $1,701 on Tuesday, many end-users will be cautious, as the price rise has been fuelled by speculative fund buying.
Meanwhile, the copper market was not seeing so much business. There was a reasonable level of enquiry and expectations of trade developing, particularly from China.
"The Chinese have the authority to buy, and they have the funds to buy," a leading copper trader noted.
But China is usually unwilling to pay prices that seem expensive or could be close to what may be perceived to be the high-point in the market's cycle, others noted.
There is no pressing reason to buy spot metal, so the Chinese may hold back for some time when the market may have settled lower.
Also, because the market was heavily backwardated in February, general business has been restricted to necessary requirements, with very little incremental trade taking place.
"A lot of people are underweight in the physical side, because the cash price was so high," the trader said.
Another factor that has inhibited trade in primary cathodes this year has been the better availability of scrap, compared to the final quarter of 1996.
Then, scrap prices reached levels equivalent to refined cathodes, whereas scrap is now at a 75 stg discount, a UK scrap trader noted.
"The signs are that it (demand) will pick up, there are pockets of interest, but it is not consistent," the scrap trader said.
Physical tin traders said that price dips towards $5,800 were potentially inducive for end-users, although because the dollar Continental end-users are holding off, a European trader said.

Lead physical indications were broadly unmoved, as the LME switch into backwardation last Friday has had little real impact, although there have been some offers of Singapore warrants at levels around $15.
"If it remains in backwardation it will affect physicals in Europe," a lead trader said.
